CAR CON 2020

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Car thieves that are so slick they con victims into willing handing over their keys without even being threatened violently.

Summary:
It’s not a new scam. But it’s an upgraded version.

Criminals con car owners into handing over the keys to their wheels under the guise of either being a dealership or more recently a tracking company. Using technology to make spoof calls and fake email addresses to con the victims that they are the real deal – it’s a much cleaner hit without guns and violence.


Further information:
THE MO
Instead of putting a gun in the victim's face and using violence and intimidation to get the car - they pose as employees from legitimate companies - victims hand over the keys and only figure out hours, if not days later that they were conned. The car thieves made off with the car with the key and a head start without any cops chasing them - the car is gone for good!

It’s a much more civilised and sophisticated tactic. Once they collect the car, they're off with the keys and at least a couple of hours to get out the tracking device.

THE RECALL CON
Earlier this year this syndicate presented itself as the manufacturer of luxury brands like Ferrari, Maserati, Lamborghini and Jaguar. They called clients claiming there was a safety issue with the car and it had to be taken in order to replace part and insure the warranty is maintained. But because they don’t want to inconvenience the clients they would come collect the car, do the repair and return it to the valued customer.

Accept once they drove off, they were never to be seen again.

TWELVE HIGH END VEHICLES WERE STOLEN LIKE THIS – some were recovered – in SA and in neighbouring countries like Mozambique, others have disappeared without a trace.

A NEW SPIN
After insurance companies warned their clients about this elaborate and costly con, the recall con died down, only to be reborn as a TRACKING ERROR SCAM. They would now contact clients purporting to be from a vehicle tracking company – they would claim there was an issue with the tracking device and they would be able to fix it on site. Same story, client hands over the keys, and they drive off into the sunset never to be seen again.

TRACK RECORD
This is a syndicate operating, there have been arrests - previously they used an insider at the service departments and would call the dealership saying a driver was going to collect the car - the dealership would hand over the car and keys to the so-called driver and the car would be gone by the time the real owner arrived to collect.

WE HAVE FOOTAGE OF ONE OF THE INCIDENTS

INSURANCE NOT PAYING OUT
Insurance company may not pay out in most cases because the clients handed over the keys….

HOW CLIENTS ARE CONNED
These syndicates have taken the storyline one step further by using soft ware to spoof calls – so it looks like the call is from the tracking company, dealership or manufacturer. We do a show and tell with a hacker to show us how it’s done and talk about possible breaches in how the information is accessed.

CASE STUDY TBC CONFIRMED – Might be hidden ID

GARTH: // just think a little bit more when you're transacting with people that you do not know. As humans, we are looking to trust people. And that's a nice thought, but it doesn't always have a positive outcome. INT2M14

PROMO1
VO: You wouldn’t think you’d just hand your car keys to a car thief. But a string of luxury vehicle owners did just that. We investigate this sophisticated scam tricking people out of their wheels.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Car thieves that are so slick they con victims into willing handing over their keys without even being threatened violently.
metadata.Summary: It’s not a new scam. But it’s an upgraded version. Criminals con car owners into handing over the keys to their wheels under the guise of either being a dealership or more recently a tracking company. Using technology to make spoof calls and fake email addresses to con the victims that they are the real deal – it’s a much cleaner hit without guns and violence.
metadata.Further information: THE MO Instead of putting a gun in the victim's face and using violence and intimidation to get the car - they pose as employees from legitimate companies - victims hand over the keys and only figure out hours, if not days later that they were conned. The car thieves made off with the car with the key and a head start without any cops chasing them - the car is gone for good! It’s a much more civilised and sophisticated tactic. Once they collect the car, they're off with the keys and at least a couple of hours to get out the tracking device. THE RECALL CON Earlier this year this syndicate presented itself as the manufacturer of luxury brands like Ferrari, Maserati, Lamborghini and Jaguar. They called clients claiming there was a safety issue with the car and it had to be taken in order to replace part and insure the warranty is maintained. But because they don’t want to inconvenience the clients they would come collect the car, do the repair and return it to the valued customer. Accept once they drove off, they were never to be seen again. TWELVE HIGH END VEHICLES WERE STOLEN LIKE THIS – some were recovered – in SA and in neighbouring countries like Mozambique, others have disappeared without a trace. A NEW SPIN After insurance companies warned their clients about this elaborate and costly con, the recall con died down, only to be reborn as a TRACKING ERROR SCAM. They would now contact clients purporting to be from a vehicle tracking company – they would claim there was an issue with the tracking device and they would be able to fix it on site. Same story, client hands over the keys, and they drive off into the sunset never to be seen again. TRACK RECORD This is a syndicate operating, there have been arrests - previously they used an insider at the service departments and would call the dealership saying a driver was going to collect the car - the dealership would hand over the car and keys to the so-called driver and the car would be gone by the time the real owner arrived to collect. WE HAVE FOOTAGE OF ONE OF THE INCIDENTS INSURANCE NOT PAYING OUT Insurance company may not pay out in most cases because the clients handed over the keys…. HOW CLIENTS ARE CONNED These syndicates have taken the storyline one step further by using soft ware to spoof calls – so it looks like the call is from the tracking company, dealership or manufacturer. We do a show and tell with a hacker to show us how it’s done and talk about possible breaches in how the information is accessed.
